title: With qualities, without
hook: the One is both beyond all qualities and present in every quality

segments.voice: Yesterday, the name Waheguru: wah, the cry of wonder, joined to Guru. Your line was wonderful lord. When did wah slip out of you, and did you let it last a breath longer? Day one thousand three hundred sixty-four.

Is God far off, or right here? Put that to a room of people and the answers tend to split. Lean too far one way, and God is a distance with no one in it. Lean too far the other, and God shrinks to a figure you could fit in a picture frame. Two answers that seem to cancel each other: God is beyond everything; God is right here, in this. Sikh scripture doesn't make anyone pick. It holds both answers in one breath, with two words that sound almost like twins. Today's word is the first of them.
screen: `FAR OFF, OR RIGHT HERE?` → `BEYOND EVERYTHING, OR RIGHT HERE?` → `TWO WORDS, ALMOST TWINS.`

segments.voice: First, nirgun. In the Granth's language, gun means a quality, a trait, the kind of thing you'd list to describe someone. Nirgun is the One without qualities: beyond every description, past anything we could name, measure or picture. No shape, no color, no edge where it stops. Second, its twin, sargun. Sargun is the One with qualities: present in every form there is, in the river and the mountain, in the stranger at the bus stop, in the patience of an old woman cooking for the langar. The same One that no word reaches is also in everything words touch. Third, the line that holds both. In Sukhmani Sahib, Guru Arjan's long hymn of peace, there's a line that says it plainly. In paraphrase: the One is without qualities, and the One is with qualities too. Not two gods. Not a far God and a near God taking turns. One, both ways at once. Sikh teachers sometimes put it with the picture of the ocean and its waves: the ocean has no single shape, and every wave is still the ocean. Fourth, why this matters on an ordinary afternoon. If the One were only beyond, you'd have to leave the world to find it. If the One were only here, it would shrink to whatever you happened to like. Nirgun and sargun together keep both doors open: awe at what no one can hold, and tenderness toward what is right in front of you. Vast and close.
screen: `NIRGUN: BEYOND EVERY QUALITY.` · `SARGUN: PRESENT IN EVERY FORM.` · `ONE, BOTH WAYS AT ONCE.` · `AWE AND TENDERNESS TOGETHER.` · then, large: `VAST AND CLOSE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: feel both vast and close. Settle, and breathe. For the first part of the sit, think of the biggest thing you can: a mountain range, a desert, all the people who have ever lived. Let it be too big to hold. Then, for the second part, bring your attention to something small and near: your own hand, the sound in the room, the next breath. If you pray, you can hold both at once as one. If you don't, just notice the shift from vast to close, and back. The bell holds the time.
Nirgun. The One without qualities, beyond every description, held together with sargun, the One present in every form. Today's word.

Your line: vast and close. Today, once, stand somewhere wide, a field, a busy street, a shoreline, and once, look closely at something small within reach, and hold them as the same thing. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: Sikhs speak of the One as nirgun, beyond all qualities, and sargun, present in every form, and Sukhmani Sahib, which holds both together, is recited by Sikhs at home and in gurdwaras.

fork.setup: a friend asks you: is God far beyond the world, or right here in it? you have to answer.
options: beyond it, so look away from the world.
right here, so there's nothing beyond.
both: beyond every quality, present in every form.
fork.reveal: Sukhmani Sahib doesn't make you choose: the One is nirgun and sargun at once.

original.note: Gurmukhi: without qualities; its twin is ਸਰਗੁਣ, sargun, with qualities.

trapdoor: what you thought: nirgun means God has no good qualities.
what it means: beyond every quality and description, held together with sargun, present in every form.
what a scholar hears: Sukhmani's line: the One is without qualities, and the One is with qualities too.
recall: one who walks on Nanak's path

notes: Paraphrase of 'nirgun aap sargun bhee ohee' (Sukhmani); please confirm the Ang (287) and the paraphrase.
The gloss of gun as 'quality' and nirgun/sargun as without/with qualities is a standard explanation, not argued as an etymology; please confirm.
The ocean-and-wave picture is introduced as an image 'Sikh teachers sometimes' use; please confirm or cut.
Gurmukhi given as ਨਿਰਗੁਣ / ਸਰਗੁਣ in modern spelling; the Granth spells ਨਿਰਗੁਨੁ / ਸਰਗੁਨੁ. Please confirm which form to show.
